newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB holds wheat pools, lowers 97/98 crop forecast.
newsitem.headline: AWB holds wheat pools, lowers 97/98 crop forecast.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Monday it held its estimated 1996/97 and 1997/98 wheat pool returns unchanged on the level set two weeks ago and had closed its 1996/97 pools.
The Board also lowered its preliminary estimate of the 1997/98 wheat crop now being planted to a range of 15 to 16 million tonnes from 18 million tonnes.
The AWB's estimate for Australian Standard Wheat (ASW) wheat remained at A$198 a tonne for 1996/97 and in a A$180 to A$190 range for 1997/98, it said.
With the closing of the 1996/97 pools, the estimated equity for future deliveries will be line with the 1997/98 pools, the AWB said.

"It has been our practice to protect the equity of existing equity holders by closing the pools when additional deliveries may adversely impact on the pool equity," AWB merchandising general manager Ron Storey said.

"Given our record crop 1996/97 crop of 24 million tonnes and the extent of the market's decline in the first half of 1997, the AWB's strategy of maximising shipments in the first half of the season has been a winner," he said in a statement.
Grower returns benefitted by more than A$100 million through this programme, he said.
Although markets have been under Northern Hemisphere harvest pressure, the AWB's medium to long term outlook remains unchanged, Storey said.
The recent improvement in U.S. production prospects as well as harvest pressure has contributed to the weakness in the market, he said.
"However, the potential impact of the El Nino phenomenon on Australian, Southern African and next year's Indian crops are expected to more than offset this," he said.
The market had focussed on U.S. production and had tended to ignore the improving demand prospects in North Africa and Western and Southern Asia, Storey said.
"Traditionally, the wheat market makes seasonal lows about this time of year, and we would expect to see prices move higher as the season progresses," he said.

Turning to the crop outlook, Storey said: "Based on the latest meteorological advice and recent weather patterns, the AWB believes Australia's 1997/98 wheat crop will be in the 15 to 16 million tonne range - in line with Australia's 10-year average."
"It is early days yet, but we cannot ignore the rainfall deficiency to date and the forecasts for below average rainfall over parts of the wheat belt during the growing season," Storey added.
The AWB's estimate has moved into line with the forecast of 16.3 million tonnes by the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) in mid-June, down from 19.2 million previously.
But on Monday, Australian Wheat Forecasters Pty Ltd held its July estimate for the wheat crop virtually unchanged on June at 17.87 million tonnes.
The wheat crop year is April-March and the marketing year October-September.
The AWB said it will issue its next pool equity update on July 21.
